Structure verified verbatim against the PDF's SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS table (page xi) and the per-theme strand tables (pages 1-55).

essenceNote: Kenya's foreign languages at Junior School are Arabic, French, German, and Mandarin — each a non-formal, basic (A1/YCT2-equivalent) 4-skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing) curriculum, taught in an experiential, innovative and flexible program guided by social-constructivism and environmental theories (verbatim essence statement, identical wording to the Grade 9 German design).

notes: Same 9 themes repeat identically across all 3 strands (Greetings and Introduction, Family, My Surroundings, Time, Fun and Enjoyment, Foods and Drinks, My Body, Weather and Environment, Getting Around) = 27 distinct sub-strands (9 themes x 3 strands), confirmed verbatim from the PDF's own SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS table and per-theme tables — an exact structural match to German's own Grade 9 design and to French's Grade 8 design (same theme set and order across all three). Total lesson allocation: 27 (Listening & Speaking) + 18 (Reading) + 9 (Writing) = 54 lessons + 6 lessons for showcasing, matching French Grade 8 exactly. Verbatim vocabulary/phrase examples pulled directly from the design's own suggested-learning-experiences tables (marked 'z.B.' = 'zum Beispiel', for example) were preserved in sub-strand names/themes where the source itself embedded them, e.g. Wie heißen Sie?/Ich heiße... (greetings), der Vater/die Oma/der Onkel/der Cousin (family), der Supermarkt/der Markt/die Bibliothek (surroundings), Wie spät ist es?/Es ist...Uhr (time), der Löwe/der Elefant/die Schlange (wild animals), Kopfschmerzen-style feelings vocabulary, Der Berg ist hoch/Der Wald ist grün (physical features), nach rechts/nach links/geradeaus-style directions.
